turns.text: Even after I close my laptop, I keep replaying work in my head. By dinner I feel flat and still a bit on edge.
On Tuesday I put some music on while I made dinner. I noticed I settled a little sooner when there was something between work and the rest of the evening.
We can try noticing how the evening feels, without aiming for a particular score. The check-in is a way to observe, rather than another task to get right.
We looked at the evenings when a work message comes in late. I usually read it straight away, and then it’s harder for me to be present at dinner.
I’ll rate my mood from zero to ten each evening around eight. I can add an energy rating if I feel like it.
I can make time for one thing I enjoy or find meaningful this week. I’ll choose what it is when I see how the week goes.
I’ll try the same breathing practice we did together once this week, for three minutes after work. I’m happy to note my tension before and after if I feel like it.
I’ll send you the recording we used. The check-in can just ask how it went.
Thursday evenings are tight because I pick up my niece. I’d like to keep that in mind.
A short journal might be worth talking about another time, if you’re interested.
Next time, can we look at whether I felt any different on the evenings when I gave myself a little time after work?
Yes, let’s compare what you noticed at our next session.
